title: Control engineering changes and recover prior states
statement: Project decision owners, engineers, and maintainers need to evolve coherent engineering states through controlled changes while preserving the ability to identify, compare, and recover retained prior states and understand their original decisions and provenance.

what.problem: Changes can obscure earlier engineering states and their provenance, while interruptions can separate unfinished work from its context and decision authority.
what.desired_outcome: Participants can identify and compare retained states, recover them with their original meaning, and continue controlled work with its recorded context and applicable authority.

why.rationale: A current model alone cannot explain how it came to exist, establish what an earlier assessment examined, or support reliable recovery of a previous engineering state. Controlled work also needs continuity after interruptions and respect for the project's decision authority.

stakeholders: Engineering agents acting within project authority

conditions: Applies when changes are proposed, assessed, adopted, corrected, or retired, and when a retained baseline is inspected or recovered. It also applies when in-progress work is interrupted, resumed, or handed to another participant.

Retain active work, unresolved findings, applicable decisions, and evidence needed for current reliance until resolved or coherently replaced. Retained baselines have no automatic age-based expiry; release of retained material is a separate controlled retention-policy decision that first resolves surviving dependencies.

contexts: Across Changes, Baselines, configuration management, and provenance in the governed engineering environment.

how.approach: Identify coherent Baselines, control transitions, and preserve recoverable states and their provenance under the selected retention policy. In the initial authoring profile, a retained baseline identifies its governed requirement and asset definitions, relationship facts, applicable metamodel and rules, source provenance, and any realization or assurance material included in its declared scope. References alone do not claim recovery of unavailable external content. On-demand recovery selects an intact retained baseline and reproduces its recorded authoritative content and meaning; unavailable or incomplete recovery is reported explicitly. Keep current work context available for resumption and distinguish project decision authority from assessment results and suggested actions; SR-006 and SR-007 elaborate these obligations.

how_much.scope: Covers Changes, Baselines, configuration management, revision provenance, and historical meaning under the project's retention policy. It does not require permanent working-tree copies, a particular version-control technology, or a specific external handoff service. Recovery applies to retained states. It also covers continuity of recorded in-progress work and human decision authority under the selected project policy, without requiring a new confirmation for every already-authorized action. Completed historical material may leave the current working view only after its original meaning is recoverable and current dependencies are reconciled. The initial authoring profile includes recovery from an available intact retained baseline, with no elapsed recovery-time commitment or storage-disaster recovery guarantee. Unsaved or unrecorded work and destruction of the retained storage are outside that guarantee.
limits: Zero loss or alteration of the selected baseline's recorded authoritative content, identities, relationships, and provenance in a recovery declared complete. This bound is relative to that baseline, not to later unrecorded work.

assumptions: The selected retained baseline and its applicable interpretation rules remain intact and accessible through the project's configuration-management arrangement.

sources.basis: Controlled transitions, identifiable baselines, recoverable states, and historical integrity.
